2027-07-19.title: Monday of the Sixteenth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today
I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously
Something greater than Jonah is here
2027-07-19.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 16 (Year I). The first readings of this week follow Israel through the Exodus: the crossing of the sea, the manna, Sinai and the covenant. The responsorial psalm is the Song of Moses (Exodus 15), given here in NRSV numbering (Lectionary 15:1bc–2, 3–4, 5–6 = NRSV 15:1–6); the same song is sung every year at the Easter Vigil. In these monsoon weeks of Kerala, with the rivers full and the roads cut off, the story of a people with the sea in front of them and an army behind them is heard with fresh ears. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-07-19.verse: But Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today you shall never see again. The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still.”
theo: Israel has walked out of slavery on the night of the Passover, and for a few days it seems that the story has ended happily. Then comes the news in Pharaoh's palace: the people “had fled,” and “the minds of Pharaoh and his officials were changed.” “What have we done, letting Israel leave our service?” The king takes “six hundred picked chariots and all the other chariots of Egypt,” the most advanced army of the age, and goes after a crowd of ex-slaves, women, children and flocks. The Israelites are camped by the sea, at Pi-hahiroth, in front of Baal-zephon, and when they look back they see the dust of the chariots. “In great fear the Israelites cried out to the Lord.” That is a good prayer. But the next words are not: they turn on Moses. “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness?” Fear can make a person forget that slavery was slavery; “it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians,” they say. Moses answers with three short commands: “Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today.” Not only the Lord's strength but his timing is announced: “today.” “The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still.” To keep still does not mean to do nothing. Immediately the Lord says to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.” There is a time to stand and trust and a time to move; faith is knowing which is which, and trusting that the God who opens a way will also tell us when to step on it. The Lord adds that he will “gain glory for myself over Pharaoh,” so that “the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord.” The reading stops before the sea opens; the psalm gives us the answer in advance, the song Israel sang on the far shore: “I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.” Jewish tradition keeps a gentle comment on this song: an old rabbinic story says that when the angels wished to sing as the Egyptians drowned, God said, “My creatures are drowning in the sea, and you would sing?” Even in victory, the God of Israel does not rejoice in the death of any human being. The Church sings this canticle at the Easter Vigil, because the sea is also a picture of baptism, and St Paul says that our ancestors “were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea” (1 Corinthians 10:2).

In the Gospel, some scribes and Pharisees say to Jesus, “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.” They have just watched him heal a man who could not see or speak (Matthew 12:22), and they have heard his teaching on the kingdom. A sign for them means a proof they can examine on their own terms. Jesus answers sharply: “An evil and adulterous generation asks for a sign.” In the prophets, “adulterous” is the word used for a people that is unfaithful to the covenant, as a spouse is unfaithful to a spouse; it is not an insult against a race. Jesus is himself a son of Israel, and he speaks as the prophets spoke to their own people, with grief and love. The Church has always taught that what was done in his Passion cannot be charged to all the Jews of that time, still less to the Jews of our own day (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 597). The only sign that will be given is “the sign of the prophet Jonah.” “For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.” Jesus points to his own death and rising, the sign above all signs. He names two figures from outside the circle of those who asked. The people of Nineveh, a pagan city, “repented at the proclamation of Jonah”; the queen of the South, a foreign monarch, “came from the ends of the earth to listen to the wisdom of Solomon.” Each of them recognised God's word when it came in a modest and costly way. “And see, something greater than Jonah is here! … something greater than Solomon is here!” In the first reading Moses stood by the sea and said, “Stand firm”; here the One greater than Moses stands among the people and gives himself as the sign. At the Red Sea God opened a path through the waters of death for Israel; in the Resurrection of Jesus he opens a path through death itself for the whole human race.
outline: Ask: when did you last feel that you had the sea in front of you and an army behind you?
Point 1 · Do not be afraid, stand firm
Moses' three commands and the God who fights for his people.
Point 2 · Tell them to go forward
Trust and action together: why do you cry out to me?
Jesus' death and Resurrection, the sign that is given; something greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.
“The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still.”
live: Write down the one difficulty that frightens you most this week, and under it Moses' words: Do not be afraid, stand firm. Pray them each morning.
After praying about that difficulty, take one small, concrete step today: make the call, begin the paperwork, ask for forgiveness.
2027-07-19.prayer: Lord God, you led your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a path for them through the sea. When we are afraid, give us Moses' faith: to stand firm, to keep still before you, and to go forward when you say go. Lord Jesus, you gave us the sign of Jonah, your death and Resurrection; through the waters of baptism lead us out of every slavery into your freedom. Make us people who sing your praise even when the way is not yet open. Amen.
altar: The story of the crossing is read every year at the Easter Vigil. Every baptism is a passage through the sea, and every Eucharist is the meal of those who have been brought through it. Jesus, the sign of Jonah, is present on the altar: the Crucified and Risen One, the gift greater than Jonah and Solomon, who tells us in the sacrament what he told the frightened disciples on the lake: Do not be afraid.

quick: Pharaoh pursues Israel to the sea; the people panic, and Moses says: Do not be afraid, stand firm; the Lord will fight for you.
The Lord tells Moses: Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
Jesus refuses a proof to those who demand one, and promises only the sign of Jonah: his three days in the heart of the earth.
2027-07-19.action: Take one small step today toward the thing you are afraid to face, after praying Moses' words.
2027-07-19.question: When I am afraid, do I only cry out, or do I also trust and go forward when the Lord says go?

family.explain: The people of Israel had left Egypt, but then they looked back and saw the king's army coming after them, and in front of them was the sea! They were very frightened. Moses said: do not be afraid. The Lord will fight for you. God made a path through the sea, and all the people walked across on dry ground. Whenever we feel there is no way out, we can remember that God made a way in the sea.
family.intention: We pray for families who are afraid or in trouble, and for people whose homes are in danger from the monsoon floods.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we afraid as a family, and how did God help us? Can we thank him tonight?”

illus: In a low-lying village near the Periyar one monsoon night, the river rose faster than anyone expected and the only road went under water. The village was frightened. An old woman who had lived through many floods went from house to house with a lamp and said the same thing at every door: do not be afraid; stay together; keep the children upstairs; I have already told the boatmen at the next bend. At first light two country boats came, and every family got across. Afterwards a neighbour asked her how she had stayed so calm. She said: my mother used to tell me what Moses said: stand firm and see what the Lord will do today. But she also said that Moses was told: go forward. So I prayed, and then I sent the boy to the boatmen. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you open a way where we see none. Lord Jesus, sign of Jonah, risen from the dead, make us stand firm and go forward in faith. Amen.
share: Do not be afraid, stand firm (Exodus 14:13). Which fear in my life most needs to hear these words?
Tell the Israelites to go forward (Exodus 14:15). Is there a step God is asking me to take while I stand wondering?
Something greater than Jonah is here (Matthew 12:41). In what way do I still ask Jesus for proof rather than trust his word?
pm.resp: I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously.
interc: For the Church, that she may trust the Lord who fights for her and go forward in mission.
For all who are afraid today: the sick, the unemployed, the people living in flood-prone places, and refugees.
For those who pass through the waters of baptism, and for their godparents and families.
For the Jewish people, who first sang the Song of Moses, and for peace among all the children of Abraham.
For our group, that we may seek not signs but the Lord himself.
pm.close: Father, you saved your people through the sea and your Son from the grave. Make us stand firm in trial and sing your praise. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, picture the scene. Israel has just left Egypt. They are camped by the sea, and then the dust cloud appears behind them: Pharaoh's six hundred chariots. In front of them the water, behind them the army. They cry out to the Lord, and then they turn on Moses: was it because there were no graves in Egypt? How quickly fear makes us forget that slavery was slavery. Have we not also spoken that way when things get difficult, wishing that we were back in the old life, even the old sin?

Moses says three things: do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today (Exodus 14:13). The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still. But look what the Lord says next: why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward. There is a time for stillness, a time for prayer, and then a time to walk into the water. God does not do for us what we can do with his help. He made a way through the sea, but the people had to put their feet on it.

In the Gospel some people ask Jesus for a sign: show us something so that we can believe. Jesus has healed and taught, and still they ask for more. He answers that only one sign will be given, the sign of Jonah: as Jonah spent three days in the belly of the sea monster, so the Son of Man will spend three days in the heart of the earth. Jesus is saying: my death and my Resurrection are the sign. Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching; the queen of the South travelled the world to hear Solomon. And something greater than Jonah, something greater than Solomon, is here.

Let us not keep asking for more proof while the Lord himself stands among us. At every Mass he gives himself to us, risen and alive. Today let us name our sea, whatever frightens us, and say with Moses: the Lord will fight for me. And then let us take one step forward. Amen.
kids: Children, a long time ago God's people were running away from a cruel king. They came to a big sea, and the king's soldiers were behind them! The people were very scared. But Moses said: do not be afraid! God will help us. And God opened the sea, and the people walked right through on dry ground! When you are scared, remember: God can make a path where there is no path. Say a little prayer, and then do the brave thing.

intro: Theme: “The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still.”
The sea in front, the army behind, and the sign that is greater than Jonah.

points.h: Do not be afraid, stand firm
q: But Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today you shall never see again.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Choose the fear that troubles you most, and say Moses' words over it every morning this week.

sub: Why do you cry out to me?
A time to stand, a time to walk.
The God who opens a path.
q: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as if it were dry land, but when the Egyptians attempted to do so they were drowned.
points.apply: After praying about your difficulty, take one practical step today, and do not wait for the whole path to be clear.

sub: Three days in the heart of the earth.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Go to Mass this week, not to ask for a sign but to receive the One who is the sign.

concl: God opened a path through the sea for Israel and told Moses to lead the people forward; he asks us for trust and for a step.
Jesus gives the sign of Jonah, his death and Resurrection; something greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.
2027-07-19.resolve: Each day this week name one fear, say Moses' words over it, and take one step.
